colonnade.rule: Every building, megastructures included, stands its ground floor on the building line (plot edge set back by streetscape.sections[class].pavement). Upper floors and decks may overhang the pavement to the plot edge only as a colonnade listed on the megastructure (megastructures[].colonnade): the section's walk zone stays clear underneath, clear height ≥ levels.headroom.colonnade, columns (levels.column) only in the frontage or kerb zone, ≥ 0.45 m from the kerb face (Manual for Streets). Malls, walks and quays carry their own bands inside the foot path: their pavement is 0 and a face on them stands on the plot edge.
colonnade.fields: colonnade[]: footprint (index into footprint), edge (x0 | x1 | y0 | y1 of that rect), faces (road or foot id), class (section class), depth (m, plot edge inward = the section's pavement), over (what overhangs: deck | upper storeys), clearHeight (m, ≥ levels.headroom.colonnade), columnZone (kerb | frontage), columnEvery (m along the edge)
colonnade.source: Rue de Rivoli arcades (1802); Bologna portici; Park Hill (1961) deck over the street edge; Manual for Streets 2007

towers.podiumGrowWhy: a tower's podium = its site rect grown one bay (buildings.bay 6), so the tower stands ≥ setback.by 6 back from the podium edge
towers.rule: Towers stand only at these sites: each closes a view (Parade axis, Market Street, Crown Avenue, the harbour). Composed, never a grid.
towers.kitRule: brief 006 B: a tower site takes a DecoKit Highrise or Skyline piece only where it fits as built: footprint inside the site rect (lower) and rect − 2 × halfBay above storey setback.above 9; body roof on the storey grid at floorTop(storeys) (the kit's 3.6 m floor = upperStorey; pivot on the podium deck 9.43 = podium top); crown tip ≤ crownTip. levels.station: A sky rail station's platforms are side platforms at concourse z 24, outer edge 8 m from the line (beamCentres/2 + 0.75 beam + 4 m platform). Each station reaches the street by ≥ 2 stair-and-escalator banks (one each side of the line) and ≥ 1 lift each side; banks land on public ground (pavement, median, mall, park, quay), never on a plot. A megastructure concourse within 30 m joins the station by a skybridge ≥ 5 m wide. Tram stops stay at street level.
levels.bridges: A deck or bridge over a road keeps headroom.road under its structure (z − structureDepth − 0.18 ≥ 5.5); its supports stand in the zones its megastructure lists, never in a carriageway or the tram reservation. A bridge crossing the sky rail line passes ≥ 3 m clear of any pylon.

frontage.source: brief 004 A1 · GDD §01 (exteriors only: a trade is a frontage) · §15 (no text on signs; palette) · Buchanan 1963 (no frontage access on primary distributors) · Gruen, Shopping Towns USA (1960) · Googie roadside commerce (Lautner, Armet & Davis)
frontage.rule: A trade is a frontage: shopfront, canopy, sign blank (shape + colour + icon, never text), door, service bay if listed, spill onto the pavement. Interiors are never modelled.

placement.never: primary distributors (Buchanan: no frontage access); building backs on a primary are blank stone with service yards behind
placement.corner: corners on two streets take an anchor trade (w ≥ 18) where the mix has one, else a diner or hotel lobby
placement.repeat: the same trade never stands side by side on one edge
placement.service: roller bays (4.5 w × 4.6 h) only on access roads, the quay or under a deck; never on a district road or the mall
placement.lobby: every building has ≥ 1 lobby on its quietest street
placement.wantsNote: 2026-10-12 (brief 006 B, Datum): walk was an allowed street that no trade wanted, so the generator relaxed onto it (F-2, 89 tenancies on Garden Walk, the Lamplight courts and Skyport Pier). A pedestrian walk is the best shop street there is (Rotterdam Lijnbaan 1953; Park Hill front doors on the deck): the neighbourhood trades and the lobby now want walk, travel-bureau too (the pier to the Skyport). Florist and soda-fountain want deck because the Crown Terraces deck mix lists them (the Terrace Walk's corner café); newsstand and florist want access (corner kiosks on side streets); diner, hotel-lobby and newsstand want park (facing the gardens); hiring-hall and robot-repair want district (Docks Boulevard). No trade gained a primary
placement.signs: colours from §15 city palette only: cream_stone, paper_cream, teal_enamel, mint_enamel, gold_trim, chrome, sky_cerulean, zenith_cobalt, warm_sand, stone_shadow, ink_black. coral_transit only on transit kiosks. vermilion, violet_set, green_circle are faction colours and signal colours are gameplay: never on a sign.

streetscape.source: brief 004 (Sky 2026-10-11: kiosks, stops, phone booths, tree-lined streets, rooftops) · GDD §05 (watchers at stations, stops, gates, squares; witness 13 m; cameras fixed visible cones blocked by roofs and parked vehicles; levels in 3D) · §09 (people from the trades on their block) · §15 (palms, chrome, coral transit, no text, signal colours never on a surface) · NACTO Urban Street Design Guide 2013 (frontage / pedestrian through / furniture zones) · DfT Inclusive Mobility 2021 (2.0 m clear path, 1.5 m at obstacles, seats 0.45–0.48, bollards ≥ 1.0 m tall) · BS 5489-1:2020 + EN 13201 (column spacing ≈ 3–4 × mounting height) · Manual for Streets 2007 (furniture 0.45 m from the kerb face) · IFC 2021 Appendix C (hydrant spacing) · Fruin, Pedestrian Planning and Design 1971 (stair speeds) · EN 115-1 (escalators ≤ 30°, 0.5 m/s, flat landings) · Seattle Center Monorail 1962 (Alweg beam 0.9 × 1.5 m) · Googie: Armet & Davis, Lautner; Litfaß column (Berlin 1855); K6 kiosk (Scott 1935)
streetscape.rule: Rules the generator applies per street edge, seeded by plot id + edge index; nothing here is placed item by item. Order per edge: section zones → transit kits → crossings + bollards → trees → lamps → watchers → catalogue items by want priority. An item that does not fit is skipped, never squeezed (SF-6). Heights are above the surface the item stands on.
streetscape.pavement: Plots run to the kerb line (plot edges meet road edges; standards.roads.frontage tolerance 1 m). The pavement is the strip of each plot between the kerb face and the building line: the building line is the plot edge set back by sections[class].pavement. A plot edge on two classes takes the wider. Civic blocks keep their own 4 m walk (civic.walk, fixed by C-0) and their own objects; this standard does not dress them.

sections.note: zones from the kerb face inward: kerb (trees, lamps, furniture; items ≥ 0.45 m from the kerb face, Manual for Streets) · walk (clear, never blocked, SF-1) · frontage (spill, vending robots, planters; spill depth = min(frontage.placement.spill.depth, this zone)). pavement = kerb + walk + frontage.

primary.median: trees + twin-boomerang lamps in the 4 m median, except along a T2 median platform (its 37.2 m + 2 m each end) and where T2 slews across the median (roads[].tram)
primary.why: no frontage on primaries (frontage.placement.never): 0.5 m plinth strip only; 3.0 walk because primaries carry the walk between areas (NACTO through zone 2.4–3.6)

tram.note: T2's cross-section wherever it runs on a primary (where: roads[].tram). Offsets in m from the road centreline, positive toward the tram's half (24 m road: median ±2, carriageway 2–12, pavement 12–17). The pair centre is 6.0 off the centreline, as drawn in tram[T2].paths.
tram.running: right-hand: the outer (kerbside) track runs with the half's traffic in the shared lane; the inner track runs contraflow in its own lane, behind a flush 0.4 m cobbled separator (surface, not an object: SF-3 holds). The kerbside 2.4 m strip is a hard strip (no frontage access on primaries), taken by the kerb platform at stops; cars queue behind a tram at a stop.

median.note: the whole 4 m median + a 0.8 m build-out into the separator and tram lane; the shelter's glazed back faces the far carriageway 0.5 m in from its kerb

kerb.note: a 2.8 m build-out over the kerbside strip, joined level to the pavement: the whole 5 m pavement rises 0.12 to the platform top for the 37.2 m stop, 1:20 along the walk at each end (2.4 m). The shelter stands across the joint in the raised kerb zone, its back 0.5 m short of the walk (13.5), so the walk keeps 3.0 and the platform keeps 2.3 clear

platforms.why: platform edge = track ± 1.4 (tramStop.edge). The 2.8 m kerb build-out alone left 1.3, so the shelter steps back into the raised kerb zone

why: Kit (brief 006 B): adopted where a piece fits as built or scales honestly (landmarks.sphere SphereStation, skyport-tower.kit.regen Skyport_Tower (portal variant; the pad in the loop is a caisson with three SkyPad_Roof), landmarks.monument CircusMonument, skyport-tower.gateway ParabolicArch, roofs hover-pad SkyPad_Roof); the five tower sites carry regen orders (Tower_Stepped ×2, Tower_Saucer, Tower_Atom, Tower_Lantern). Rejected: SpaceHQ (252 m, no HQ in the district, would outrank the Skyport 2.3 ×), LinerDock (205 m gantry, 68 m square, no berth), Skylon (108 m, wants a 26 m way and outranks every park band), DiscTower (44 m floorplate, 157 m), SkyBridge (72 m span at 60 m between towers 88 m apart; our bridges are 14–48 m deck and concourse connectors), Tower_Starburst / Needle / Terrace / Setback (tips 121–196 m on the podium, no site left; Needle 34 m saucer, Setback 30 m plan with no crown to spare), SkyRailStation (rail top 22 and 40 m single-beam platforms vs 24 and 50 m side platforms on twin beams: regenerate).
Tram: one track (x −2.5) in a 16 m street from z −40, ending 6 m short of the circus. No loop, no crossover, no second track, one stop island; the line starts and ends nowhere.

Sky rail: a closed loop 24 m up the west promenade, straight over the tram street, round the Sphere station at r 88, then diagonally back across the west city with pylons dropped onto whatever is underneath.
Harbour line: a second closed loop on the quay with a balloon round the skyport (R 48). It shares no station with the sky rail or the tram.

Roads: the street kit is one straight street and a side street. The map graph (harbour-map.json) links the civic block to Comet Row and Sunset Way by two exit roads; nothing defines the district's road hierarchy or where those roads go.
concept: Buchanan's hierarchy: a primary ring (Sunset Way, Crown Road, Harbour Road, Comet Row) carries through traffic round the district; district distributors (the Boulevard, Market Street, Circus Road, Crown Avenue) feed it; access roads serve seven environmental areas and never link two distributors.
Every way a car can enter an environmental area is a gate. For a mission, the gates are the seal points; the Records Precinct has two.

Crown Circus is the hub (EPCOT 1966: a radial centre with transit through it). Four arms: the Boulevard south, Crown Avenue north, Circus Road west, Crown Parade (a pedestrian mall) east to the harbour.

Tram T1 runs in the Boulevard's central reservation with stops about 300 m apart. It turns on a balloon loop round the circus island (R 28), so single-ended trams need no crossover. South of Comet Row it runs on to Southside.

Sky rail S1 is the airport line (Tokyo 1964). One straight trunk: Skyport, Harbour, Crown Circus, Sphere Gardens, then the West End. It runs over public space only: the Parade, the circus island, Circus Road's median and the Skyport Pier. Trains turn on a loop over the water round the skyport pad; the Skyport station stands on the pier's apron, the landside end.
The two systems cross at right angles at Crown Circus, the one interchange (sky station to tram stop ≈ 120 m).
The Records Axis: the Sphere Gardens sky station, Garden Walk, the café, the fountain, the raised table on Orbit Walk and the office door all sit on x = −160.

Players cross any road anywhere. Kerbs, medians, the tram reservation and the circus are walkable ground (no guard rails); crossings and raised tables only calm traffic. Walking distances on this sheet are measured that way: round buildings and water, straight over streets.
questions: Scale: 1.1 × 1.1 km with seven environmental areas. Keep that, or plan only the Records Precinct and Lamplight for the slice and leave the rest as massing?
Tram: terminate on the circus loop (as drawn), or run on up Crown Avenue to Crown Road?
Sky rail: one straight trunk replaces the Sphere loop and the separate harbour line. OK to retire both?
Names: Comet Row is now the south ring road (it was the Boulevard's continuation). Rocket Lane is the getaway street; Satellite Street, Starline Street and Orbit Gardens are reused. Keep them?

Records Precinct: two vehicle gates (Rocket, Satellite) to seal against cars, but on foot the crew can leave across any street. Is the escape on foot meant to be open like that, with the police sealing stations rather than streets?

sources: C. Buchanan et al., Traffic in Towns (HMSO, 1963): distributor hierarchy, environmental areas, no frontage access on distributors.
W. Disney, EPCOT film (1966): radial hub, transit spine, segregated levels.
Alweg / Seattle Center Monorail (1962): beams about 0.9 × 1.5 m; spans ≤ 30.5 m straight, 22.9 m at R ≥ 183 m, 18.3 m at R < 91 m.
Tokyo Monorail (1964): the airport line; Hitachi straddle monorail minimum radius 70 m (large type) and 40 m (small type).
Tram practice: running radius ≥ 50 m, ≥ 25 m at junctions and terminal loops (18 m absolute, Riga); stops 300–500 m apart; track centres 3.2–3.8 m.
V. Gruen, Shopping Towns USA (1960); Southdale (1956); Fort Worth plan (1956): stacked pedestrian galleries over service, cars kept to the edge.

A. & P. Smithson, Golden Lane (1952); Lynn & Smith, Park Hill, Sheffield (1961); Barbican highwalks: decks as streets, wide enough for a milk float; Brunswick Centre (1972) and Habitat 67 (1967): terraces over a podium.
R. Banham, Megastructure (1976): the 1960s megastructure as city infrastructure with plug-in uses.
Googie and roadside modern (Lautner; Armet & Davis), LAX Theme Building (1961), Seattle Space Needle (1962): sign as shape, saucer towers.

openQuestions.question: Is the wait for the next service the full headway, the average (half headway), or modelled from the mission clock?
openQuestions.why: The GDD says price = wait + ride from the timetable but does not define how the wait is computed.

openQuestions.question: Is there a walking pace, and does boarding count the interchange walk as part of the price?
openQuestions.why: The GDD states no walking pace; 1.4 m/s is an [S] assumption for interchange walks.

openQuestions.question: Can a boarded vehicle be seen, stopped or sealed (e.g. Alert 3 closing stations)?
openQuestions.why: The timetable assumes continuous service; the GDD travel rule does not cover closures. The plan notes police sealing stations rather than streets.

openQuestions.question: Does T2 run in both directions, and does a rider choose the shorter way round?
openQuestions.why: The GDD does not say; journeys here assume either direction on the line.
